name: sweet potato turnip pie
instructions:
The ATK vegetable pot pie line (split from the former sweet-potato-pies-and-galettes house): cremini mushrooms + sweet potato + turnips + swiss chard filling, roux-based gravy, crust on top. The vegetable stack is right, and the gravy secret is found: LEMON JUICE + ZEST and PARMESAN at the finish (see the breakthrough note). Crust: [[atk-galette-dough]] (whole wheat, white vinegar).

=== PROCEDURE (ATK SCAFFOLD) ===

1. Roll pie dough to a 10-inch circle, crimp the edge, cut four 2-inch vents, refrigerate. Oven to 400°F.
2. Sauté onion + cremini mushrooms in butter until the mushrooms release their liquid (~5 min).
3. Add sweet potato + turnips (1/2-inch pieces), cover, cook until edges soften (7-9 min). Add garlic; cook 30 seconds.
4. Wilt in the swiss chard (~2 min); transfer everything to a bowl.
5. Gravy: butter + flour roux, whisk in the liquid (see salvage plans), simmer to thicken. Off heat, whisk in lemon juice.
6. Recombine, transfer to a deep-dish pie plate, top with the vented crust, egg wash, bake ~30 min at 400°F until golden and bubbling. Cool 10 min.
notes:
=== THE ISSUES — GRAVY FAILURES (ALL DECIDED) ===

The ATK vegetable stack (sweet potato + turnips + chard + mushrooms) is right, but the gravy has failed in every configuration tried:
- ATK'S VEGETABLE BROTH: light enough to let the vegetables shine (that's why they chose it) but makes a very awkward gravy.
- DARK VEGETABLE BOUILLON: CLASHES. Decided.
- GARDEN VEGETABLE BOUILLON: CLASHES — tasted fine but turned the gravy MOSSY GREEN once the roux thickened it. Decided.
- GINGER: CLASHES. Decided — the old lemon+ginger+smoked-paprika profile is dead.
- Stronger stocks (chicken/beef bouillon) just turned it into a suboptimal chicken/beef pot pie where the veggies don't shine.

THE BREAKTHROUGH COOK — LEMON + PARMESAN IS THE SECRET: tried a chicken-pie-style gravy (white wine, cream, rosemary + thyme + sage), leeks swapped for onion, chard left out. It DIDN'T land as well as a chicken pot pie... until the ATK finishers went in: LEMON JUICE + ZEST and PARMESAN CHEESE — they helped ENORMOUSLY, and that seems to be THE SECRET. Historically I skipped the parmesan and swapped lemon for ginger — that was WRONG. ATK is right: the FUNKINESS OF PARMESAN + BRIGHTNESS OF LEMON is the correct axis for this pie.

Other findings from that cook:
- SAGE did a lot for savoriness; THYME did a little; ROSEMARY was orthogonal (the nothing-to-grip pattern again).
- HALF A STALK OF CELERY made it WORSE — celery clashing.
- LEEKS alone weren't enough; ONION POWDER helped — ONION NEEDS TO BE THERE.

NEXT COOK: try again with the CHARD + ONION back in, alongside the mushroom/sweet potato/turnip stack, keeping the lemon + parmesan finish.

=== POT-PIE ERA LESSONS (KEPT) ===

- TURNIPS + SWEET POTATOES are the identity pair — earthy-bitter root + sweet/savory counterweight.
- DON'T CHICKEN OUT ON SWISS CHARD quantities — greens wilt to a third of their raw volume.
- ATK'S VEGETABLE REJECTIONS: no asparagus, no leeks — army-green and overcooked by the time the crust browns.
- TOO MUCH LEMON: the sauce reduces in the oven and concentrates it — season under, let the oven concentrate.
- PANKO OVER REGULAR BREADCRUMBS if doing a crumb top instead of crust.
- CRUST VENTING: cut vents while the dough is flat, before it goes on.
- PORCINI POWDER worked as the parmesan substitute in the old gravy — moot if the cheese-binder salvage direction wins, since real parmesan comes back.

=== WANT TO TRY ===

- The FULL-STACK COOK: chard + onion back in alongside mushroom/sweet potato/turnip, with the lemon + parmesan finish (queued as the next cook).
- Cheese-binder variations if the gravy still wants less liquid: cream cheese, monterrey jack.

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- [[atk-galette-dough]]: the crust.
